verdicts.evidence: agents/qa.md:52-58 — "**Check for clean working tree (full mode only):**" / `git status --porcelain` (:55) / ":58 If dirty, **STOP** and ask the user/orchestrator: commit the changes, stash them, or abort — each bug fix needs its own atomic commit on a clean tree."
verdicts.reasoning: Verified both sides at the claimed lines. KICKOFF:764-766 tells the operator to run the same command, states the same consequence (agent stops on a dirty tree), and gives the same justification ("every fix it makes needs its own atomic commit") — the skill's Setup gate re-derived almost word for word, with the option set narrowed from commit/stash/abort to commit/stash. The only genuine delta is timing (pre-flight instead of mid-run), which is why this is medium and not high: it saves a wasted unattended dispatch. But it adds no parameter, path, or condition the skill lacks — the skill already knows it needs a clean tree before it starts.

verdicts.evidence: agents/qa.md:251 — "Skip if: not \"verified\", OR purely visual/CSS with no JS behavior, OR no test framework exists."; and :262 "...still failing → delete and defer; >2 min exploration → skip and defer."
verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF:788 promises "a regression test per fix" with no qualifier; Phase 8e.5 skips the regression test for best-effort and reverted fixes, pure visual/CSS fixes, projects with no framework, and any test costing more than two minutes. Those are common QA cases (visual findings are one of the agent's own scoring categories at :205), so the guide sets an expectation the skill will routinely not meet — an operator could read a missing test as a failure. Confirmed as a scope overstatement rather than a head-on behavioral conflict, hence low; it is subsumed if qa-7's tier prose is trimmed, since it lives in the same sentence.
